source: Rules written for the Toolkit from Mateusz Dąbrowski’s SFMC SQL guides (mateuszdabrowski.pl), in our own words

rules: List columns by name; never SELECT *.
Alias every computed column with AS, named like the target field.
No LIMIT: use SELECT TOP n. Pair TOP with ORDER BY so the rows kept are predictable.
DISTINCT compares all selected columns; for one row per key use ROW_NUMBER.
From a child BU, read shared, synchronized or parent data views with the Ent. prefix, e.g. Ent.Contact_Salesforce, Ent._Subscribers.
Do not use Ent. in the parent BU itself, and do not read another BU's DE by MID prefix.
Find non-matches with LEFT JOIN and WHERE joined_key IS NULL, or NOT EXISTS.
Join _Sent to _Open, _Click, _Bounce, _Unsubscribe on JobID, ListID, BatchID and SubscriberID together.
Add IsUnique = 1 on engagement joins or one send fans out into many rows.
Join _Sent to _Job on JobID; join to _Subscribers or a DE on SubscriberKey.
UNION removes duplicates, UNION ALL keeps them; each part needs the same column count, order and types.
Test missing values with IS NULL / IS NOT NULL; = NULL and != NULL never match.
A comparison like Flag != 'True' drops NULL rows; use ISNULL(Flag, 0) = 0 or add OR Flag IS NULL.
NOT IN returns nothing if the list or subquery holds a NULL; prefer NOT EXISTS.
LIKE: % any run, _ one char, [abc] set, [^abc] not in set; literal % is [%].
Boolean DE fields are BIT: compare with 1 or 0 (text 'True'/'False' also converts).
_Subscribers.Status is text: 'active', 'unsubscribed', 'held' or 'bounced'.
GETDATE() and data view dates are CST (UTC-6) all year; GETUTCDATE() is UTC.
Relative ranges: EventDate >= DATEADD(DAY, -7, GETDATE()).
Whole days: compare with CONVERT(DATE, GETDATE()) using >= start and < next day. Avoid BETWEEN on datetimes.
To show local time: TODATETIMEOFFSET(d, '-06:00') AT TIME ZONE 'Pacific Standard Time'. Use standard zone names.
AT TIME ZONE returns DATETIMEOFFSET; CONVERT it back to DATETIME before writing to a Date field.
Text to date: CONVERT(DATE, txt, 103) for dd/mm/yyyy, 101 for mm/dd/yyyy, 120 for yyyy-mm-dd hh:mi:ss.
DATEDIFF counts boundaries crossed (Mar 31 to Apr 1 is 1 MONTH). DATEPART returns a number, DATENAME text.
CONCAT treats NULL as empty; a + b returns NULL if either side is NULL. Use CONCAT or COALESCE.
String positions start at 1. CHARINDEX returns 0 when not found, so guard LEFT/SUBSTRING lengths.
Email domain: SUBSTRING(Email, CHARINDEX('@', Email) + 1, 254) with WHERE Email LIKE '%@%'.
STRING_SPLIT and OPENJSON fail the syntax check; do not use them.
Never type an N prefix before text literals and never use double quotes for text; use single quotes.
INT / INT drops decimals: multiply by 100.0 or CONVERT to DECIMAL(18, 2) before dividing.
Guard division by zero with NULLIF(denominator, 0).
DE Number fields are INT and cut decimals; target a Decimal field or ROUND first.
Give DECIMAL a precision, e.g. DECIMAL(18, 2). Avoid FLOAT and REAL.
Prefer CONVERT(type, value, style) over CAST: only CONVERT accepts a date style code.
One bad value fails the whole run; use TRY_CONVERT, which returns NULL instead.
Find bad rows with TRY_CONVERT(type, col) IS NULL AND col IS NOT NULL.
Use searched CASE WHEN condition THEN value ... ELSE value END; always add ELSE.
CASE returns the first WHEN that matches, so put the most specific conditions first.
IIF(condition, if_true, if_false) is fine for a single test.
Every non-aggregated selected column must be in GROUP BY.
Filter rows with WHERE before grouping; filter groups with HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.
COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(col) and COUNT(DISTINCT col) skip NULLs. AVG and SUM ignore NULLs.
One row per key: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY EventDate DESC) AS rn in a subquery, then WHERE rn = 1 outside.
ROW_NUMBER needs ORDER BY inside OVER. Add a unique tiebreaker column so reruns pick the same row.
Random groups: NTILE(2) OVER (ORDER BY NEWID()). Results change every run, so store them in a DE.
COUNT(DISTINCT x) OVER () is not allowed; count in a grouped subquery and join it back.
Email name and subject come from _Job joined on JobID.
Journey of a send: _Sent.TriggererSendDefinitionObjectID = _JourneyActivity.JourneyActivityObjectID, then _Journey on VersionID.
_Subscribers in a child BU shows that BU only; use Ent._Subscribers for all.
JSON_VALUE(col, '$.key') returns text up to 4,000 characters; use JSON_QUERY for objects or arrays.
Guard with IIF(ISJSON(col) = 1, JSON_VALUE(col, '$.key'), NULL): broken JSON fails the run.
Output column names must match target DE fields; unmatched columns are silently dropped.
Overwrite replaces all rows, Update upserts by primary key, Append adds rows.
Append fails on any primary key the target already has or the query repeats; dedupe first.
Fill every required target field and primary key; COALESCE NULLs to a default or exclude the rows.
Text longer than the target field fails with truncated: cut with LEFT(col, n) to the field length.
Filter data views by EventDate inside the subquery or WHERE before joining them.
Narrow large sources in a subquery first, or split into several query activities writing to staging DEs.
Avoid functions on join keys and LIKE in ON clauses; they slow joins a lot.

core: Write one T-SQL SELECT statement for SQL Server. SFMC runs only SELECT: no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DECLARE, variables or temp tables.
Never use WITH (CTEs): write a subquery in FROM with an alias instead.
No semicolons. No -- comments; if a comment is needed, use /* */ without apostrophes.
No LIMIT, NOW(), IFNULL() or double-quoted text: use TOP, GETDATE(), ISNULL() and single quotes.
Do not add ORDER BY unless the query also has TOP or OFFSET.
Every output column needs a name: alias expressions with AS to match target DE field names.
Use only the given tables and fields; never invent fields.
Wrap names with spaces or hyphens in [brackets].
Data views and GETDATE() are Central Standard Time (UTC-6), no daylight saving.
Data views keep roughly six months of data.
Window functions and aliases cannot be used in WHERE; wrap them in a subquery.
When joining, alias every table and prefix every column.
Queries over 30 minutes are stopped: filter large data views by date early.

examples.request: Subscribers who opened any email in the last 30 days
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.SubscriberKey
FROM _Open AS o
WHERE o.EventDate >= DATEADD(DAY, -30, GETDATE())
    AND o.IsUnique = 1

examples.request: People sent the email named Spring Sale in the last 7 days who did not open it
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT s.SubscriberKey
FROM _Sent AS s
INNER JOIN _Job AS j
    ON j.JobID = s.JobID
LEFT JOIN _Open AS o
    ON o.JobID = s.JobID
    AND o.ListID = s.ListID
    AND o.BatchID = s.BatchID
    AND o.SubscriberID = s.SubscriberID
    AND o.IsUnique = 1
WHERE j.EmailName = 'Spring Sale'
    AND s.EventDate >= DATEADD(DAY, -7, GETDATE())
    AND o.SubscriberID IS NULL

examples.request: The most recent click per subscriber with the URL
examples.sql:
SELECT
    ranked.SubscriberKey
    , ranked.URL AS LastClickedUrl
    , ranked.EventDate AS LastClickDate
FROM (
    SELECT
        c.SubscriberKey
        , c.URL
        , c.EventDate
        , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.SubscriberKey ORDER BY c.EventDate DESC, c.JobID DESC) AS rn
    FROM _Click AS c
    WHERE c.EventDate >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, GETDATE())
) AS ranked
WHERE ranked.rn = 1

examples.request: Open rate per email for sends in the last 14 days
examples.sql:
SELECT
    j.EmailName
    , COUNT(*) AS SentCount
    , COUNT(o.SubscriberID) AS OpenCount
    , CONVERT(DECIMAL(18, 2), COUNT(o.SubscriberID) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)) AS OpenRate
FROM _Sent AS s
INNER JOIN _Job AS j
    ON j.JobID = s.JobID
LEFT JOIN _Open AS o
    ON o.JobID = s.JobID
    AND o.ListID = s.ListID
    AND o.BatchID = s.BatchID
    AND o.SubscriberID = s.SubscriberID
    AND o.IsUnique = 1
WHERE s.EventDate >= DATEADD(DAY, -14, GETDATE())
GROUP BY j.EmailName

examples.request: Rows from the Orders DE placed yesterday
examples.sql:
SELECT
    OrderId
    , SubscriberKey
    , OrderDate
    , Total
FROM Orders
WHERE OrderDate >= DATEADD(DAY, -1, CONVERT(DATE, GETDATE()))
    AND OrderDate < CONVERT(DATE, GETDATE())

examples.request: Email addresses used by more than one contact in the shared Members DE, from a child BU
examples.sql:
SELECT
    m.Email
    , COUNT(*) AS ContactCount
FROM Ent.Members AS m
WHERE m.Email IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY m.Email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

examples.request: Active subscribers with a full name and a label for gmail, outlook or other domain
examples.tables: _Subscribers data view, Profile DE (SubscriberKey, FirstName, LastName)
examples.sql:
SELECT
    sub.SubscriberKey
    , sub.EmailAddress
    , TRIM(CONCAT(p.FirstName, ' ', p.LastName)) AS FullName
    , CASE
        WHEN sub.Domain = 'gmail.com' THEN 'Gmail'
        WHEN sub.Domain IN ('outlook.com', 'hotmail.com') THEN 'Outlook'
        ELSE 'Other'
    END AS MailboxProvider
FROM _Subscribers AS sub
LEFT JOIN Profile AS p
    ON p.SubscriberKey = sub.SubscriberKey
WHERE sub.Status = 'active'

examples.request: Which journey and email each send came from today
examples.sql:
SELECT
    s.SubscriberKey
    , s.EventDate AS SentDate
    , jb.EmailName
    , jr.JourneyName
    , jr.VersionNumber AS JourneyVersion
FROM _Sent AS s
INNER JOIN _Job AS jb
    ON jb.JobID = s.JobID
LEFT JOIN _JourneyActivity AS ja
    ON ja.JourneyActivityObjectID = s.TriggererSendDefinitionObjectID
LEFT JOIN _Journey AS jr
    ON jr.VersionID = ja.VersionID
WHERE s.EventDate >= CONVERT(DATE, GETDATE())

examples.request: Copy the Import Staging DE into Customers, converting the text birth date (dd/mm/yyyy) and skipping rows without a key
examples.tables: Import Staging DE (Id, Email, BirthDateText), target Customers (CustomerId PK, Email 254, BirthDate Date)
examples.sql:
SELECT
    st.Id AS CustomerId
    , LEFT(st.Email, 254) AS Email
    , TRY_CONVERT(DATE, st.BirthDateText, 103) AS BirthDate
FROM [Import Staging] AS st
WHERE st.Id IS NOT NULL
